title: Gavin C Probable NDE 7122
content: On a rafting trip in the head waters of the Waioi River, our raft containing six people flipped over in a grade 4 rapid. In the final moments before our raft hit the wall, at about 50 kilometers per hour and being the strongest member of the crew and super-human, I tried in vain to fend off the wall. The angle of the boat changed, as we hit, and drove the oar straight into my pelvis. It took 4 days for the above information to come back to me. At the time, I remember the raft flipping and me being in white water but incapacitated. I came up, hit my head on the underside of the upturned raft and took a breath of water. I choked, took another breath and everything went calm. I exited the white water into calmer water. I was in a starfish-position with my legs down, floating about mouth height. The water had a strange ripple in the center and I slowly started to sink. I knew I was about to die but there was nothing I could do, I couldn't move. Under the water, it was a grey color and I continued to descend, I was looking for the rock that was creating the turbulence that was dragging me down. I couldn't understand why I was descending but there was no fear or panic, the water was very warm considering mind the river was ice melt. I then spotted the cave that the water was going into; it made sense now the river was going under the earth. I was mesmerized by it. Suddenly, I was startled by two large bangs and pictures of my two little girls flashed before me. I suddenly realized what was happening and it was the end, I went absolutely crazy kicking fighting and obviously came-to under water. I don't remember the accident, just popping out of the river unable to breathe. Every time I coughed, water poured out of my throat I could only breathe back a tiny amount, I couldn't breathe out. I couldn't talk. I was floating too low in the water, so I tried rolling onto my back: anything to give me the chance to get air. I could see the rescue kayaker but couldn't call him. I hit a shallow gravel bar in the river and thought it would give me time to recover but it was like I was a rag doll; I bashed and smashed over it. At about this point, I decided to relax and possibly drown again because it was too hard to swim. I knew I must have been close to the other boats looking to rescue us. I figured I had up to 8 minutes for my body to be resuscitated so prepped myself. In one last attempt, I got my hand straight up and made a sound. The rescue kayaker suddenly appeared beside me and told me to grab on, I grabbed the grab handles with pinpoint precision. I don't remember the trip to shore or being dragged out of the water. I remember them asking me if I had seen the others. I thought I was talking but obviously not. They then realized my lungs were full of water and had a discussion about how they were going to get the water out of my lungs, as I'm a 100 kg body builder they were never going to be able to hold me upside down. Hypothermia set in fast but I didn't realize it, I felt warm and numb. My whole body had cramped and I was in shock and hyperventilating. They got me up and moving, which was a feat in itself, as I couldn't move a muscle. No emergency services were called, as no one realized what had happened they thought I had taken a couple of gulps of water and was exhausted. After the flip over, they had done a head count and couldn't find me, they presumed I was under the raft. I was under the river.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Raft flipped in a grade 4 rapid; oar driven into pelvis; head hit underside of raft; drowning/aspiration of water.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Experience described as drowning/descending into grey underwater cave (river going under earth), calm/no fear; then two loud bangs and images of his two little girls flashed, which startled him and triggered frantic struggle and resurfacing.

“I choked, took another breath and everything went calm.”
“Under the water, it was a grey color and I continued to descend…”
“I knew I was about to die… there was no fear or panic…”
“Suddenly, I was startled by two large bangs and pictures of my two little girls flashed before me.”
